h1: The 6 Best Garden Augers for Bulbs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Garden Augers for Bulbs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 bulb augers scored on diameter, shaft length, drill drive and soil fit, from a four-size set to a 3 inch planter.
summary: The MAXCCINO 4-Piece Auger Set is the one to buy if you plant more than one kind of bulb, because it spans 1.6 to 3 inch holes. The MAXCCINO 2x14.5 is the better single tool for daffodils and tulips. Gardeners with big bulbs or stubborn ground should look at the Power Planter DIY Guru 3x12, while the long 1.6x16.5 augers suit crocus, grape hyacinth and other small bulbs planted deep.
intro: Most bulb augers are bought for the wrong dimension. Shoppers compare length because it sounds like depth, then discover the hole is too narrow for a hyacinth or too wide for a row of crocus. Diameter decides which bulbs an auger can serve, and the drill you own decides whether it works at all. A 3/8 inch drive chucked into a weak drill will stall in clay and burn out the battery.

We ranked six augers by reading their spec sheets against how bulbs are actually planted. Scoring leaned on diameter range, shaft length for planting depth, drive type, and how well the spiral design clears soil rather than packing it back down. Every pick here is under $25, so the ranking is about fit and soil, not price.

products.name: MAXCCINO 4-Piece Auger Set
products.verdict: Four sizes from 1.6 to 3 inches cover every bulb you are likely to plant.
products.description:
The set ships as 1.6x8.6, 3x12, 2x14.5 and 2.6x16.5 inch augers, all with a 3/8 inch non-slip drive and an 18V or higher drill recommended. That spread matters because bulb size varies far more than most gardeners expect: a crocus corm and a large hyacinth bulb need very different holes.

It tops the list because no single-size auger here can match the range. The 2.6x16.5 handles deep tulip and lily planting, while the short 1.6x8.6 suits shallow crocus drifts. The cost is carrying four tools, and the thinnest bit will not clear dense clay as fast as the wide ones.

Buy it if your beds mix small and large bulbs, or if you are unsure what you will plant next autumn. Skip it if you only ever plant one variety.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who plant mixed bulbs in one autumn session.
products.skipIf: You plant a single bulb type and want one dedicated tool.

products.name: MAXCCINO 2x14.5 Bulb Auger
products.verdict: The 2 inch bore that fits daffodils and tulips, with enough length for proper depth.
products.description:
This is the 2x14.5 inch size pulled out of the set above: a 2 inch diameter spiral, 14.5 inches long, on a 3/8 inch non-slip drive. A 2 inch hole is the sweet spot for medium bulbs like daffodils and tulips, which sit comfortably in it without a lot of backfill.

It ranks second because it does one job well and costs less than the set. What it gives up is flexibility: at 2 inches it is too tight for hyacinth-sized bulbs and oversized for tiny crocus. The 3x12 Power Planter below digs a wider hole but a shorter one.

Choose it if daffodils and tulips make up most of your planting. Pair it with an 18V drill, since the maker advises that power level for the spiral to clear soil without bogging.
products.idealFor: Daffodil and tulip planters who want one dependable tool.
products.skipIf: You plant both tiny and oversized bulbs.

products.award: Best for Large Bulbs and Tough Soil
products.name: Power Planter DIY Guru 3x12 Auger
products.verdict: A 3 inch bore built for big bulbs and listed for clay, rocky soil and sand.
products.description:
At 3 inches wide and 12 inches long, this is the widest hole in the ranking, and the listing names dirt, clay, rocky soil and sand as suitable ground. It is also sold for mixing paint and cement, a hint that the spiral is sturdy enough to turn something thicker than loam.

It sits third because width trades against depth. Twelve inches is shorter than the 14.5 and 16.5 inch augers above, which limits you for deep-set tulips or lilies, and a 3 inch hole wastes effort on small bulbs. Against the MAXCCINO set, you get one size instead of four.

Best for amaryllis, large alliums and anyone planting in compacted beds. The caveat is that the specs do not list a drive size, so confirm your chuck fits before buying.
pros: Listed for clay and rocky soil
products.idealFor: Large-bulb planting in clay or rocky beds.
products.skipIf: You need holes deeper than a foot.

products.name: NAFOGAR 2-Pack Auger Set
products.verdict: A narrow 1.6 inch and a wide 3.5 inch auger for gardeners at both ends of the size range.
products.description:
The pair is a 1.6x16.5 and a 3.5x16 inch auger on a 3/8 inch hex drive, with no drill included. Choosing the two extremes is a smart bit of packaging: the thin one handles crocus and snowdrops, the wide one takes the largest bulbs.

It lands fourth because the middle is missing. Neither bit suits a standard 2 inch daffodil hole particularly well, and the MAXCCINO set fills that gap with four sizes. Both NAFOGAR shafts are at least 16 inches, though, which gives more reach than the Power Planter.

A reasonable buy for gardeners who plant small spring bulbs and a few giants. The hex drive grips more securely than a round shank, but you still need your own drill with enough torque for the 3.5 inch bit.
products.idealFor: Planting crocus drifts plus a few oversized bulbs.
products.skipIf: Daffodils and tulips are your main crop.

products.name: TCBWFY 1.6x16.5 Bulb Auger
products.verdict: A solid-shaft steel auger with extra spirals for deep, narrow holes.
products.description:
This one is a 1.6 inch diameter by 16.5 inch long auger built on a solid shaft of heavy-duty steel with extra spiral turns and a black paint finish. The solid construction is the point: a narrow, long bit is prone to flexing, and a solid shaft resists that.

It ranks fifth because 1.6 inches limits which bulbs it can plant. Crocus, muscari, snowdrops and similar small bulbs fit well, but daffodils crowd the hole. Against the Sproot, which has the same dimensions, the TCBWFY is the one with the tougher shaft description, though the paint finish will chip with use.

Pick it for naturalising small bulbs in lawns or borders where depth matters more than width. Do not expect it to double as an all-round tool.
products.idealFor: Deep planting of crocus and other small bulbs.
products.skipIf: You grow daffodils, tulips or hyacinths.

products.name: Sproot 1.6x16.5 Bulb Auger
products.verdict: An extended-spiral, 3/8 inch hex auger that matches the TCBWFY dimensions.
products.description:
The Sproot is a 1.6 inch by 16.5 inch auger with an extended spiral and a 3/8 inch hex drive. The longer spiral is meant to lift more soil on the way out, which helps in loose ground where cuttings would otherwise fall back into the hole.

It finishes last because it offers the same size as the TCBWFY and the NAFOGAR's narrow half without any extra feature to separate it. The listing does not mention a solid shaft or a coating, so durability is an open question. If both narrow augers cost the same, the TCBWFY's heavy-duty steel description gives it the edge.

A workable pick for small-bulb planting if you want the hex drive and a long spiral. Buy it only if you are certain narrow holes are all you need.
products.idealFor: Small-bulb planting in loose, workable soil.
products.skipIf: You want the proven heavy-duty option or a wider bore.

methodology.title: Diameter range
methodology.description: A bulb auger is only useful if its hole fits the bulb, so we scored how many common bulb sizes each pick can plant.

methodology.title: Shaft length
methodology.description: Length sets planting depth, and many spring bulbs need 6 to 8 inches of soil above them, so longer reach scored higher.

methodology.title: Drive and drill fit
methodology.description: We checked drive shape and the recommended drill voltage, since a hex or non-slip shank that slips wastes the whole tool.

methodology.title: Soil handling
methodology.description: Spiral design and shaft construction were judged against clay, rocky and sandy ground, where cheap augers bog down.

methodology.title: Value within the field
methodology.description: Every pick is under $25, so we compared how much range and build each one delivers for that money.

whatMatters.detail: Diameter is the width of the hole and the single spec that decides which bulbs fit. Small corms need about 1.6 inches, medium bulbs about 2 inches, and large ones 3 inches or more. Measure your bulbs across their widest point, then add roughly half an inch of clearance when comparing against the listed size.

Bulbs are planted at roughly three times their own height, so tulips and daffodils often want 6 to 8 inches. Length must exceed that depth because the spiral loses efficiency near the top. Check the listed overall length, and remember that part of it sits inside your drill chuck.

A 3/8 inch hex or non-slip shank locks into the chuck and resists spinning free under load. Wide augers in clay can stall a small drill, which is why the MAXCCINO listings advise an 18V or higher drill. Check your drill's chuck size and torque setting before ordering.

The spiral lifts loosened soil out of the hole. An extended or double-turn spiral clears more, but in sticky clay it can still pack. Run the drill at low speed with steady pressure, withdraw often, and look for listings that describe the spiral rather than just the length.

A narrow, long auger can flex or bend if it hits a stone, and painted coatings chip over time. A solid steel shaft, like the one described for the TCBWFY, holds shape better than hollow tube. Look for words like solid, heavy-duty or steel in the listing rather than vague durability claims.

howToChoose.intro: Start with the bulb in your hand, because width decides everything else.

cards.label: One auger
cards.text: Cheaper and quicker to store, and fine if one bulb type dominates your planting. Picks: MAXCCINO 2x14.5, TCBWFY 1.6x16.5, Sproot 1.6x16.5 or Power Planter 3x12.

cards.label: A set
cards.text: Covers different bulb widths without compromise, which saves buying a second tool next year. Picks: MAXCCINO 4-Piece or NAFOGAR 2-Pack.

howToChoose.note: Default to the MAXCCINO 4-Piece set unless you are certain you only plant one bulb size.

howToChoose.subheading: For Clay or Rocky Soil Specifically

faq.q: Will a bulb auger work in a cordless drill?
faq.a: Yes, if the drill is 18V or higher, as the MAXCCINO listings advise. Weaker drills stall in clay. The NAFOGAR 2-Pack is sold without a drill, so check that your chuck accepts a 3/8 inch hex shank first.

faq.q: What is the most common bulb auger mistake?
faq.a: Buying for length alone. A 16.5 inch auger like the TCBWFY digs deep but only 1.6 inches wide, so it cannot take a daffodil or tulip bulb cleanly. Match diameter to bulb width first, then check length.

faq.q: Is the MAXCCINO 4-Piece set worth it over a single auger?
faq.a: If you plant more than one bulb type, yes. The set spans 1.6x8.6 to 2.6x16.5 inches, while the single 2x14.5 covers only medium bulbs. For one variety, the single auger saves money and storage space.

faq.q: How do I use an auger to avoid hurting my wrist?
faq.a: Set the drill to its low-speed, high-torque range and keep it upright. Let the spiral do the cutting rather than pushing hard. Stop and lift out soil regularly. Wide augers like the Power Planter 3x12 can kick if they hit a stone.

faq.q: How do I clean and store a bulb auger?
faq.a: Knock off caked soil, rinse, and dry the steel fully before storing, because damp soil rusts painted augers like the TCBWFY. A light wipe of oil on the spiral helps. Keep sets together so the matching bits stay organised.

faq.q: Can I use a bulb auger in a lawn or hard ground?
faq.a: Narrow models like the Sproot 1.6x16.5 are used to plant small bulbs in lawns, since the plug of turf can be replaced. In dry compacted ground, water the area first and choose the Power Planter 3x12 for its clay and rocky soil listing.

finalTake: For most gardeners the MAXCCINO 4-Piece Auger Set is the right purchase, because bulb sizes vary more than any single auger can cover. If daffodils and tulips dominate, the MAXCCINO 2x14.5 is the cleaner buy. Clay and large bulbs call for the Power Planter DIY Guru 3x12, and small-bulb specialists will like the long, narrow TCBWFY. Whichever you choose, confirm your drill is 18V or higher before the first autumn weekend.
